Marcus — thanks for the summary and the term sheet. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement/legal: 

1) When you say "logically isolated reserved pool", does that mean a fully single-tenant physical pool, or a shared host with logical controls (namespaces, network policies)? We need to know whether other tenants will ever share CUDA resources.
2) For tenant separation: we require VPC-level network separation (no public-facing endpoints), customer-provided KMS for key control, and audit logs with at least 180 days retention. Can Redwood support these?
3) Throughput SLA: can you provide the test methodology and the remedy if Redwood misses the 99th percentile target? We need a clear penalty or credit clause for the contract.

Procurement and legal are CC'd — please send an updated SOW and the technical note you mentioned. We’ll aim to have comments back in 48 hours after receiving the SOW and technical details.

Hi Sara / team,

Following up with the technical note on pool segmentation (see attached architecture-note-pool-segmentation.md). Summary highlights: 

- Isolation model: GPUs provisioned as a reserved pool and not placed on the general scheduling pool. Execution runs on dedicated CUDA contexts tied to BlueLeaf jobs — no co-scheduled CUDA contexts from other customers. The control plane remains multi-tenant for manageability but does not expose tenant-level data to other customers.
- Network & VPC: we support PrivateLink endpoints or dedicated VPC peering. Endpoints for inference ingress/egress can be configured to be internal-only.
- KMS & encryption: customer-managed KMS is supported for model artifact encryption at rest; TLS + mTLS for in-flight. Logs can be routed to your S3 bucket or to Redwood's audited store with 180/365 retention options.
- Throughput SLA testing: we base the guaranteed baseline on steady-state measured inferences/min with a fixed 512-token payload using our standard benchmark harness. Contract language will specify a 14-day measurement window post-deployment for baseline verification.
- Remedies & fallback: remedies are service credits tied to sustained SLA breaches (Mina will propose exact credit percentages). For availability issues, automatic fallback to a previously verified compatible model variant will happen with traffic throttling and immediate notification to the BlueLeaf ops contacts. We also provide a 2-week warm-up period where initial cold-cache behavior is expected; Redwood will run pre-warm workloads to reduce this effect.

Attachment: architecture-note-pool-segmentation.md

Happy to go through this on the call; available Tue 2026-04-06 10:00-11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Karhtik Iyer
